clue.text: Uninvited dinner guest fails to finish extremely elegant meal

indicators.note: the guest's name loses its final letter, so it does not reach its end

parts.note: Banquo's ghost turns up unbidden at the feast in Shakespeare's Macbeth

indicators.note: the extremes of the word elegant are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A gatecrasher leaves a fancy dinner before the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails to finish' trims BANQUO to BANQU; 'extremely elegant' gives ET.
explanation.definitionFit: A feast is a grand, elaborate meal.

clue.text: Dude … good upper-class English accent!

parts.note: dude and bro are both slang for a mate
U is the crossword letter for upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims admiringly at a posh English way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish or Scottish brogue is a regional lilt of speech.

clue.text: Declare Number Ten initially provided backing for Treasury

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word Ten

parts.note: provided, as in 'provided that', means if

indicators.note: the back of the word Treasury is its last letter

explanation.surface: Downing Street announces support for the Treasury.
explanation.walkthrough: Number Ten is Downing Street, the PM's residence; here the words split into NO and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To notify is to announce or formally inform, a synonym of declare.

clue.text: Where Orpheus was desperately lured down to embrace lover at last

indicators.note: the shuffled letters close around the extra letter, embracing it
desperately suggests the letters of lured down are flung about wildly
at last points to the final letter of the word lover

explanation.surface: The mythical musician is tempted below to hold his beloved Eurydice once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperately' rearranges LURED DOWN; 'to embrace' puts R, the last letter of 'lover', inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Orpheus went down to Hades, realm of the dead, to bring back Eurydice.

clue.text: Forename of golfer whose driving is iffy?

definitions.text: Forename of golfer whose driving is iffy?

parts.words: Forename of golfer whose driving is iffy
parts.note: a famous golfer whose driving off the tee is strong but who crashed his car on the road, so his road driving is iffy

explanation.walkthrough: The golfer is Tiger Woods; 'driving' means both hitting off the tee and motoring, and he had well-publicised car crashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger Woods is the golfer's familiar first name.

clue.text: Support retail outlet stocking engineers uniform

indicators.note: a shop stocking goods holds them inside, so the word for the shop goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a shop is a retail outlet
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A clothing store selling engineering workwear is propped up.
explanation.definitionFit: To shore something up is to prop or bolster it.

clue.text: Chaotic chaos, limb broken!

indicators.note: the broken letters of chaos and limb are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A scene of disorder ends with someone's arm or leg snapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges CHAOS and LIMB together.
explanation.definitionFit: Shambolic is British slang for disorganised and messy.

clue.text: Womble spending time in Siberian city

indicators.note: spending the time means using it up, so the letter for time goes from the name

parts.note: Tomsk is one of the Wombles, furry litter-pickers of a British children's TV series

explanation.surface: A children's TV character takes a holiday in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wombles are a British children's TV series; Tomsk is also a Siberian city, which makes OMSK a neat find once T goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Omsk is a large city in south-western Siberia on the Irtysh river.

clue.text: Depict naked US writer beginning to mould literary opus

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the word Depict loses its outer letters

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer

indicators.note: the beginning of the word mould is its first letter

explanation.surface: An artist portrays an American author unclothed, starting to sculpt a great work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' strips DEPICT to EPIC; 'beginning to mould' gives M.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic poem is a long narrative work of verse, a major literary undertaking.

clue.text: Go south-east, transporting family dog

indicators.note: transporting means carrying, so the outer letters hold the family word inside

parts.note: go is a euphemism for urinate, to pee
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: A household heads off towards the south-east, bringing along their pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb of travel but is a euphemism for urinating; 'transporting' carries the family inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pekinese is a small long-haired toy breed of dog from China.

clue.text: Chose newspaper feature about leader of Tories

indicators.note: about means around, so the feature goes around the other letter

parts.note: an op-ed is an opinion piece in a newspaper

indicators.note: the leader of the word Tories is its first letter

explanation.surface: A column in a paper profiles the Conservative leader's choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Opted means decided on or picked, a synonym of chose.

clue.text: Big Ears tickled about car feature

indicators.note: the phrase Big Ears tickled is about the answer, which lies inside it across the words

explanation.surface: A Noddy character is being tickled, all about a part of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Ears is Noddy's bearded friend in Enid Blyton's children's books; the answer runs across 'biG EARS TICKled'.
explanation.definitionFit: The lever used to change gear is one part of a car's controls.

clue.text: There to be won — bar Group F, poor second

indicators.note: poor means badly formed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A football tournament where everyone but Group F is open, and Group F finishes a poor runner-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a football draw; 'poor' is the anagram signal over 'bar Group F', not a verdict on the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available for anyone to take is up for grabs.

clue.text: Tin containing hollow pasta, nine inches

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the symbol wraps around the other letters

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

indicators.note: hollow means emptied of its middle, leaving the first and last letters of the word pasta

explanation.surface: A can of macaroni measures under a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is the old measure from thumb tip to little-finger tip, about nine inches.

clue.text: Ornamental plot rodent and kangaroo only half destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
only half of the word kangaroo is used, its first four letters

explanation.surface: A rat and a kangaroo partly ruin a garden bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' takes KANG from kangaroo; 'destroyed' rearranges that with RODENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot garden is a formal bed laid out in interlacing hedges and herbs.

clue.text: Tatty small folder containing new work attributed to Defoe

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the shuffled letters hold the extra one
tatty means scruffy and worn, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A shabby little folder holds a newly discovered manuscript credited to the author of Robinson Crusoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tatty' rearranges SMALL FOLDER; 'containing' places N from 'new' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Moll Flanders is the 1722 novel by Daniel Defoe about a woman's life of crime.

clue.text: Quickly sell Ikea's hottest curtains

indicators.note: curtains hang around and conceal, so the words sell Ikea's hottest screen the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Retail advice: sell the furniture store's best-selling curtains.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in 'selL IKEAS HOTtest'; 'curtains' looks like the product being sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something like a shot means doing it at once, without hesitation.

clue.text: Mass upset, disorder in Napoleon's place of exile

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the whole assembly is read from the bottom up
in places the disorder word inside the island's name

parts.note: Napoleon was exiled to the Mediterranean island of Elba in 1814
a mess is a state of disorder

explanation.surface: Turmoil on the island where Napoleon was exiled upsets a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts MESS in ELBA, giving ELBMESSA; 'upset' turns it upside down. 'Mass' looks like the church service but is the verb, to gather.
explanation.definitionFit: To mass and to assemble both mean to gather together in a group.

clue.text: Societal conflict … that might be brought to a head?

definitions.meaning: a struggle between social strata, workers against owners

definitions.text: that might be brought to a head
definitions.meaning: a fight in a school classroom might be reported to the head teacher

explanation.walkthrough: 'brought to a head' usually means reaching a crisis; here the head is the head teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A clash between social strata, and also a scrap between pupils in a school class, both fit the phrase.

clue.text: Young settlement known for its brackish water?

definitions.text: Young settlement known for its brackish water?

parts.words: Young settlement known for its brackish water
parts.note: Young is not new but Brigham Young, the Mormon leader who founded a town beside a salty inland lake

explanation.walkthrough: 'Young' looks like 'newly founded' but is Brigham Young, who led the Mormons to Utah in 1847.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah's capital, founded by Brigham Young, takes its name from the nearby salty lake.

clue.text: Trinket drug smuggler stashed in wings of aircraft

indicators.note: stashed in means hidden inside, so the smuggler goes inside the other letters
the wings of the word aircraft are its first and last letters

parts.note: a mule is someone paid to carry drugs across a border

explanation.surface: A courier hides a lucky charm in an aeroplane's wings.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a small charm worn for protection, a kind of trinket.

clue.text: Dirty place to see Aunt Sally skipping foxtrot?

indicators.note: skipping means leaving out, so a letter goes from the fairground word

parts.note: Aunt Sally is a traditional British fairground game of throwing sticks at a dummy's head
F is Foxtrot in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A grubby fairground where an aunt sits out the ballroom dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aunt Sally' reads as a relative; it is a fairground throwing game. 'skipping' drops one F from FUNFAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty play is unfair play, against the rules.

clue.text: Cow exposed tongue

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its outer layer, so the breed name loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow

explanation.surface: A cow sticks its tongue out.
explanation.walkthrough: Erse is an old name for Irish or Scottish Gaelic; 'tongue' means language.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland, and tongue means language.

clue.text: Game defender among sick after catching malaria at the front

indicators.note: after places the rearranged part behind the defender word

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football or rugby

indicators.note: catching means taking in, so the rearranged letters hold the extra one
sick means unwell or twisted, so the letters of among are rearranged
at the front picks out the first letter of the word malaria

explanation.surface: A footballer falls ill after picking up malaria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' looks like a link word but is the fodder that 'sick' rearranges; 'after' sets that part behind the defender.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game played with dice and counters.

clue.text: Props this country up with parties

indicators.note: up in a down clue means reading the letters upwards, so they are reversed

parts.note: this country, in a British paper, is the UK
dos are parties or celebrations

explanation.surface: A nation is supported by its political parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Props' is slang for respect or credit, not supports.
explanation.definitionFit: Props is slang for due respect, and kudos means praise or acclaim.

clue.text: Small island's looking up after removing old eyesore

indicators.note: looking up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, so reversed
the island word has a letter taken out before it is turned

parts.note: an eyot is a small river island

explanation.surface: A tiny island looks better once old stuff is cleared away.
explanation.walkthrough: An eyot (also ait) is a small island in a river, a word mostly met in Britain and in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid; the clue's eyesore puns on a sore eye.

clue.text: Spellbound wife longed to pursue vacuous brickie

indicators.note: to pursue means to follow, so these pieces come after the bricklayer's letters
vacuous means empty, so brickie loses its middle letters

parts.note: itched means longed or craved

explanation.surface: A wife yearns to chase an empty-headed bricklayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacuous brickie' is BE, its first and last letters; W and ITCHED pursue it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bewitched means being enchanted, held under a magic charm.

clue.text: Letter delivered at last terribly late

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word delivered
terribly means badly, so the letters of late are mixed up

explanation.surface: A postal letter finally arrives, awfully overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: D from 'delivered at last', then ELTA from LATE rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Serious composer established limits

indicators.note: limits means bounds, so the abbreviation goes around the composer

parts.note: Thomas Arne was an English composer, author of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A solemn musician sets firm boundaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means grave and sincere in manner.

clue.text: "Start to scrap European Alliance" — Republican politician

indicators.note: the start of the word scrap is its first letter

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance

explanation.surface: A Republican lawmaker urges pulling out of Europe's military pact.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator sits in a senate, an upper legislative chamber.
